fields.System.Title: RPL-4 — Demand-driven replenishment
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Replenish before the shortage instead of after it, by reading what the upcoming waves will
consume.

Scope

In. Reading wave demand, replenishing ahead of a wave, prioritising wave-blocking tasks.

Out. Forecasting beyond the order book. This uses known demand, not predicted demand.

Design notes

This is the upgrade that turns replenishment from reactive to proactive, and it is the
reason [RPL-2](RPL-2-reactive-replenishment.md) is built first and left alone for two stages.
Reactive replenishment running in production produces the data — how often pick faces run dry,
how long refills take — that tells you whether this is worth building and how far ahead to look.

It creates a real dependency on outbound. Replenishment must read wave contents, which is
a cross-module service call. Keep it a call, not a shared table.

A demand-driven task and a reactive task for the same location must not both exist. The
duplicate prevention from
[RPL-204](../../stories/RPL/RPL-204-prevent-duplicate-tasks.md) has to cover both sources.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Duplicate tasks from two trigger sources | [doc 09 §7.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Over-replenishing on waves that are later cancelled | [doc 05 WF 5](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Competing with allocation for bulk stock | [doc 09 §7.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
